headline: Olongapo Declares State of Calamity After Weeks of Severe Flooding
seoTitle: Olongapo Declares State of Calamity After Severe Flooding | FMB News
seoDescription: Olongapo City approved Resolution No. 196, Series of 2026, declaring a state of calamity after prolonged rain caused flooding, damage and displacement.
deck: The City Council approved Resolution No. 196, Series of 2026, placing Olongapo under a state of calamity after prolonged rainfall caused widespread impacts.
author: FMB News Desk

continuation.title: 1,395 Olongapo Residents Evacuated as Habagat Flooding Worsens
continuation.whatChanged: Olongapo moved from evacuation and flood response to a formal citywide state-of-calamity declaration under Resolution No. 196, Series of 2026.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The Olongapo City Council approved Resolution No. 196, Series of 2026 on September 1, formally placing the city under a state of calamity after prolonged rainfall caused widespread flooding, landslides, property and infrastructure damage, displacement and service disruptions.
The action followed a recommendation from the Olongapo City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council through Resolution No. 2026-04 adopted during an emergency meeting on August 31.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: FMB News first reported the city’s large-scale evacuation on August 29. The later declaration marks a new legal and operational stage in the local response rather than a correction to that earlier report.
Independent reports said Olongapo recorded about 2,900.5 millimeters of rainfall during August, roughly 3.47 times its normal August rainfall.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: A state-of-calamity declaration allows faster mobilization and use of available local disaster resources for response, relief, recovery and rehabilitation while communities remain affected.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for updated evacuation totals, road and slope conditions, relief operations, infrastructure assessments and how the city uses disaster funds for recovery and rehabilitation.
